REAL MADRID TRAINING GROUND / 02

MASTER THE GAME.

Three simple drills for first touch, dribbling and shooting. Practice technique slowly before raising the pace.

01 / FIRST TOUCH

CONTROL THE BALL

Open your body, cushion the pass with the inside of your foot, and take your first touch away from pressure. Practice 20 touches with each foot against a wall. Watch Unisport: Improve your first touch ↗

02 / DRIBBLING

BEAT YOUR MARKER

Approach at a controlled speed, sell a shoulder feint, push the ball past the defender's front foot and accelerate. Start with cones 2 meters apart. Watch English dribbling tutorials by 7MLC ↗

03 / SHOOTING

FIND THE CORNER

Plant your standing foot alongside the ball, keep your head steady, strike through the center with your laces and follow through toward your target. Watch Unisport English shooting tutorials ↗

04 / STEPOVER

THE STEP-OVER

Circle your foot around the ball without touching it, shift your body to sell the fake, and accelerate the other way.

05 / BODY FEINT

SELL THE FAKE

Drop your shoulder, commit your weight to one side, and explode toward the opposite side.

06 / SOLE ROLL

ROLL AND ESCAPE

Roll the ball sideways with the sole of your foot, then push off into open space.

KNOW YOUR GAME / 03

THE RULES OF PLAY.

LAW 11

OFFSIDE

An attacker in an offside position can be penalized when involved in active play after a teammate plays the ball; simply standing offside is not an offense. No offside offense directly from a throw-in, goal kick or corner kick.

LAW 12

FOULS & CARDS

Careless direct-free-kick fouls lead to a direct free kick. Reckless challenges may earn yellow cards; excessive force can mean a red card.

LAW 14

PENALTIES

A penalty is awarded for certain direct-free-kick offenses inside the defender's own penalty area. The kick is taken from the penalty mark.

LAW 17

CORNERS

When a defender last touches the ball before it crosses their own goal line without a goal, the attackers get a corner kick.

Official IFAB offside law ↗

Handball: not every touch of a ball by a hand or arm is an offense. A direct-free-kick handball offense inside the defending team's penalty area results in a penalty. These are simplified explanations; see official IFAB Laws.

HOW IT WORKS

YOU CALL THE PLAY.

Choose a player role, a corner/free kick/penalty or open-play scene, and late-match score. Write actions like pass into the middle, cross, shoot, dribble, or hold. Players, defenders and the ball move between decisions. A successful pass gives the receiver the next turn.

Commands use a transparent rule-based parser, not live AI. It recognizes common English and Vietnamese expressions but cannot understand unrestricted tactical language. Feedback and outcomes are simplified teaching examples rather than realistic game predictions.

The play finishes on a goal, turnover or the final whistle. No account, tracking or API key is required.
